marks.gloss_en: Rava: a cloak over a chest is like a vessel within a vessel
תא שמע: המשמשת וראתה נדה צריכה טבילה ורבי יהודה פוטר -- she is like a baal keri who saw ziva, and R' Yehuda exempts; שמע מינה
תני רבי חייא בהדיא: בעל קרי שראה זיבה צריך טבילה, ורבי יהודה פוטר -- the case the iba'ya asked about, taught explicitly
a woman who had relations and saw menstrual blood is like a baal keri who saw ziva
R' Yehuda: a zav who saw keri is exempt from immersion

according to R' Yehuda, a baal keri who saw ziva is exempt from immersion -- asked as: he exempted the zav who saw keri because from the outset that man was not fit for immersion; the baal keri who saw ziva was fit from the outset -- does he obligate him, or is there no difference?
איני?! והא אמר רפרם בר פפא אמר רב חסדא: עומד אדם כנגד בית הכסא ומתפלל -- if before-him needs full-sight distance for prayer, how may one pray facing a privy?
הכא במאי עסקינן -- בבית הכסא שאין בו צואה (= p_okimta_ein_bo_tzoah). Itself attacked and displaced at 26a.4; the surviving harmonization is the chain through p_okimta_chadtei
one may stand facing a privy and pray
איני?! והאמר רב יוסף בר חנינא: בית הכסא שאמרו אף על פי שאין בו צואה -- an empty privy is still a privy, so the empty-privy harmonization fails; conceded (אלא) and replaced by the new-privy okimta
the privy the Sages spoke of -- even with no feces in it; and the bathhouse they spoke of -- even with no person in it

והא מיבעי ליה לרבינא: הזמינו לבית הכסא מהו, יש זימון או אין זימון -- the new-privy okimta seems to settle what Ravina left open (source is the QUESTION q_hazmana, not a prop -- an objection sourced from a dilemma has no source slot)
כי קא מיבעי ליה לרבינא למיקם עליה לצלויי בגויה, אבל כנגדו לא -- the dilemma concerned praying INSIDE it; facing it is permitted either way (= p_ravina_scope)
he designated a structure as a privy: does designation take effect (to forbid) or not?
how far must one distance himself from them and from feces? four cubits
Persian privies, though they hold feces, are considered as sealed (built on an incline; the feces rolls away underground)
דאמר רבי יוחנן: ותיקין היו גומרים אותה עם הנץ החמה (no SupportKind names דאמר)
כי תניא ההיא לותיקין -- the baraita speaks of the vatikin (= p_okimta_levatikin)
when that [baraita] was taught, it was for the vatikin
תא שמע: טעה ולא התפלל מנחה מתפלל ערבית שתים, ואין בזה משום דעבר יומו בטל קרבנו
R' Yochanan: one who erred and did not pray mincha prays two in arvit, and there is nothing here of 'its day passed, its sacrifice is void'
דיקא נמי, דקתני ביטל ולא קתני טעה -- שמע מינה
ורמינהו: מצותה עם הנץ החמה -- the mishnah allows until midday, the baraita puts its mitzva at sunrise
the baraita: its mitzva is with sunrise
וכולי עלמא עד חצות ותו לא? והאמר ... רבי יוחנן: טעה ולא התפלל שחרית מתפלל במנחה שתים -- so the morning prayer can be said after midday
R' Yochanan: one who erred and did not pray arvit prays two [prayers] in shacharit
כולי יומא מצלי ואזיל -- he may pray all day; 'until midday' is the limit of the reward of prayer in its time, after which he has the reward of prayer only
he goes on praying [the morning prayer] all day
מיתיבי: מעות לא יוכל לתקן -- זה שביטל ... תפלה של ערבית או תפלה של שחרית: a neglected prayer cannot be made up
the baraita: 'the crooked cannot be made straight' (Eccl 1:15) -- this is one who neglected the evening Shema and the morning Shema, or the evening prayer or the morning prayer
אמר רבי יצחק אמר רבי יוחנן: הכא במאי עסקינן -- שביטל במזיד (= p_okimta_bemeizid)
R' Yochanan: here we are dealing with one who neglected deliberately
the morning prayer [may be recited] until midday

one who erred and did not pray mincha -- may he pray two in arvit? [arvit into shacharit may be because it is one day (Gen 1:5); but prayer is in place of a sacrifice, and when its day has passed its sacrifice is void; or perhaps, since prayer is mercy, he may pray whenever he wishes]
the evening prayer has no fixed [time]
